skill.name: dependency-updater
skill.description: Smart dependency management for multiple languages. Detects project type, applies minor and patch updates, prompts for major upgrades, and supports security audits.
skill.summary: Detects project ecosystems, updates dependencies by version risk, and runs package security audits.
skill.author: softaworks

security_audit.summary: Most Markdown backtick findings are false positives caused by code fences, tables, or documentation links. Real risks remain because the skill and helper scripts run local package managers, can fetch unpinned tools, and include emergency reset commands that delete dependency artifacts. No prompt injection text or data exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.suggestion: Restrict scripts/check-tool.sh to an allowlist of expected tool names or remove dynamic command invocation.
Require explicit user confirmation and backup guidance before running rm-based reset steps.

remediation.issue: Unpinned tool installation and npx usage
remediation.suggestion: Pin tool versions or document checksum and trust expectations before installing global tools.
Require a dry-run summary before write actions such as taze write mode, npm audit fix, pip-review auto mode, or Maven version rewrites.

semantic_findings.title: Dynamic Helper Command Execution
semantic_findings.description: scripts/check-tool.sh accepts a tool name from its first argument and invokes that value with a version flag. Quoting reduces shell injection risk, but arbitrary local tool execution remains possible if the helper is called with untrusted input.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The script directly assigns TOOL_NAME from $1 and later uses it as the command name. The behavior is visible in one short helper file, but intended allowlisted usage lowers confidence from very high.

semantic_findings.title: Destructive Emergency Reset Commands
semantic_findings.description: The instructions include rm-based resets for Node.js, Python, and Go dependency state. If an agent follows these during diagnosis without confirmation, it can delete lock files, virtual environments, and module checksum files.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The deletion commands are explicit in both the skill instructions and README. They are legitimate recovery steps, but the data-loss impact is clear if run automatically.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned Tool Installation Recommendations
semantic_findings.description: The skill recommends global or one-time installation of dependency tools without version pinning. Fetching latest tool code during a dependency update workflow adds supply-chain risk.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The installation commands are plainly documented and several install latest versions from package ecosystems. No malicious registry or domain is shown, so the risk is supply-chain exposure rather than confirmed abuse.

content.value_statement: Dependency updates are slow and risky across different ecosystems. This skill detects project types, applies safe updates, and guides audits with language-specific commands.
actual_capabilities: Detects common package files for Node.js, Python, Go, Rust, Ruby, Java, and .NET projects.
Classifies fixed, patch, minor, and major dependency version changes.
Provides workflows for taze, pip-review, go, cargo, bundler, Maven, and dotnet commands.
Uses ecosystem audit tools such as npm audit, pip-audit, govulncheck, cargo audit, and bundle audit.
Prompts for major updates and skips intentionally pinned versions.
Includes helper scripts to check tool availability and run taze for Node.js projects.
limitations: It relies on local package manager CLIs and optional audit tools being installed.
It cannot guarantee every update is backward compatible, so tests remain required.
It may change dependency manifests and lock files when update commands run.
It does not replace human review for major upgrades or security exceptions.

use_cases.title: Routine Application Maintenance
use_cases.description: Keep project dependencies current while separating safe patch updates from risky major upgrades.

use_cases.title: Maintenance Pull Request Preparation
use_cases.description: Prepare dependency update branches with changed files, audit output, and a clear verification checklist.

use_cases.title: Dependency Vulnerability Triage
use_cases.description: Run ecosystem audit tools and prioritize vulnerable dependencies by severity and remediation path.

prompt_templates.title: Check My Project
prompt_templates.prompt: Detect the project type in this repository and list outdated dependencies. Do not change files yet.

prompt_templates.title: Apply Safe Updates
prompt_templates.prompt: Update only patch and minor dependencies, skip pinned versions, then summarize changed files and versions.

prompt_templates.title: Review Major Updates
prompt_templates.prompt: Scan for major dependency updates, explain likely breaking changes, and ask me about each package before editing.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Multi-Ecosystem Repository
prompt_templates.prompt: Detect each package ecosystem in this monorepo, run the relevant audit tools, apply approved fixes, and produce a verification checklist.

output_examples.input: Update dependencies in this Node.js app.
output: Detected Node.js using package.json and npm.
Applied safe minor and patch updates.
Found two major updates and requested approval before changing them.
Ran the package audit and reported remaining issues.

output_examples.input: Diagnose my failing Python dependency install.
output: Detected a Python project using requirements.txt.
Checked installed packages and dependency conflicts.
Suggested a clean virtual environment only after explaining file impacts.

output_examples.input: Audit this monorepo for vulnerable dependencies.
output: Ran the relevant audit tools for each ecosystem.
Grouped findings by severity and listed follow-up verification steps.

best_practices: Commit lock files before and after dependency changes.
Review changelogs and migration notes before approving major updates.
Run tests and security audits after every update batch.
anti_patterns: Auto-approving every major update without review.
Deleting lock files without understanding the recovery plan.
Ignoring audit findings after dependency updates.

faq.question: Does this skill support every programming language?
faq.answer: It supports the listed ecosystems through their package files and local package manager tools.

faq.question: Will it automatically apply major updates?
faq.answer: No. The workflow prompts for major updates because they can include breaking changes.

faq.question: Can it run security audits?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses ecosystem audit tools such as npm audit, pip-audit, govulncheck, cargo audit, and bundle audit.

faq.question: Does it install required tools automatically?
faq.answer: It documents install commands and checks prerequisites, but tool installation depends on the agent and user approval policy.

faq.question: What files can change during updates?
faq.answer: Dependency manifests and lock files can change when write-mode update commands or install commands run.

faq.question: Is it safe for production repositories?
faq.answer: Use it on a branch, review major updates, commit lock files, and run tests before merging changes.
